proposed_comments.title: Keep the resize predicate helper out of the public API

confidence.rationale: The helper is introduced as public and its call sites are the production capture path and the unit tests; test-only access can be granted without expanding the public API.

proposed_comments.body:
### Keep the resize predicate helper out of the public API

**Severity:** `medium`

`IsResizeRequired` is only needed by `GetThumbnailImpl` and the unit tests, but this PR adds it as a `public` method. That unnecessarily exposes an implementation detail as a supported API surface.

Make it `internal` and grant `Preview.SvgThumbnailProvider.UnitTests` access with `InternalsVisibleTo` in the project file. This keeps the helper testable without making it part of the production public API.

proposed_comments.title: Make the resize condition easier to verify

confidence.rationale: The pinned implementation uses a compound mixed-dimension expression; the validated rewrite expresses the longest-side and pixel-format checks directly.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make the resize condition easier to verify

**Severity:** `low`

The combined dimension predicate is hard to audit and makes it easy to miss the intended rule that the longest side must equal `cx` before an ARGB image can skip resize. Compute the longest side once, then compare it and the pixel format explicitly.

```suggestion
            int longestSide = Math.Max(image.Width, image.Height);
            return longestSide != cx || image.PixelFormat != PixelFormat.Format32bppArgb;
```

proposed_comments.title: Cover premultiplied alpha in the resize predicate tests

confidence.rationale: The predicate normalizes every non-ARGB pixel format, but the new data rows do not include the distinct premultiplied-alpha format.

proposed_comments.body:
### Cover premultiplied alpha in the resize predicate tests

**Severity:** `low`

`IsResizeRequired` accepts only `Format32bppArgb`, and the test matrix covers `Format24bppRgb` and `Format32bppRgb` but not `Format32bppPArgb`. Add a PArgb row with an expected value of `true` so the non-ARGB normalization rule remains covered.

```suggestion
        [DataRow(256, 256, PixelFormat.Format32bppRgb, true)]
        [DataRow(256, 256, PixelFormat.Format32bppPArgb, true)]
```
